Error Transform Behavior

Error Transform Behaviors provide an authoritative extension point within the Error Stage that allows FeatureCells to modify, enrich, or replace the VaultErrorShape before it is committed to state and exposed to observers.

Error transform behaviors participate directly in the error-handling pipeline and are evaluated as part of error finalization. Unlike callbacks, which are observational, transforms are permitted to produce a new VaultErrorShape that becomes the active error for all downstream processing and final state commitment.

Error transform behaviors execute only after core error normalization has completed and before the error is committed to state. This guarantees that all transforms operate on a canonical error shape while preserving a single, authoritative error outcome.

Add-on Error Transform Behaviors

In addition to core error normalization, FeatureCells may opt into add-on error transform behaviors. These behaviors participate directly in the Error Stage and are permitted to transform the current VaultErrorShape before it is committed and exposed.

Error transform behaviors execute after core error normalization and before state commitment and callback execution. Each transform receives the raw thrown error, the current VaultErrorShape, and an immutable state snapshot. Based on this input, a transform may return a new VaultErrorShape or VAULT_NOOP to preserve the existing value.

Unlike callbacks, error transform behaviors are authoritative. When a transform returns a new VaultErrorShape, that value becomes the active error for all subsequent transforms and for final error state commitment.

Error transform behaviors must not throw, must not mutate state, and must not attempt to resume or suppress error finalization. Any exceptions raised by a transform are isolated, logged, and do not interrupt downstream error handling.

Note

Multiple error transform behaviors may be composed. When configured, they execute sequentially in the exact order they are declared in the FeatureCell definition. Each transform receives the current VaultErrorShape produced by the preceding behavior—starting with core error normalization—and may replace it or pass it through unchanged.

Because transforms are applied cumulatively, their order is semantically significant. Error transform behaviors should remain narrowly scoped and intentional. Overlapping or order-dependent transforms can obscure error provenance and complicate failure analysis.

Configuration

The transform contract returns unknown to allow domain-specific error representations. When a transform returns a non-VAULT_NOOP value, that value becomes the active error payload for subsequent error handling and for state commitment.

Error Transform Examples

Example 1: Register a Custom Error Transform Behavior

{{`
// ------------------------------------------------------------
// Custom Error Transform Behavior
// ------------------------------------------------------------

@VaultBehavior({
  type: BehaviorTypes.ErrorTransform,
  key: defineBehaviorKey('Addon', 'TagEmployeeError'),
  critical: true
})
export class withEmployeeErrorTagTransform<T>
  extends AbstractErrorTransformBehavior<T> {

  async transformError(
    error: unknown,
    current: VaultErrorShape,
    state: StateSnapshotShape<T>
  ): Promise<unknown | typeof VAULT_NOOP> {

    // Replace the error with an enriched version
    return {
      ...current,
      message: \`[Employees] \${current.message}\`,
      metadata: {
        ...current.metadata,
        feature: 'employees'
      }
    };
  }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------
// FeatureCell Configuration
// ------------------------------------------------------------

export const employeeCell = FeatureCell<Employee[]>(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    initialState: [],
  },
  [
    withEmployeeErrorTagTransform
  ],
  [
    // opt-in Controllers 
  ]
);

// Initialize the FeatureCell
employeeCell.initialize();

// Any error thrown in this FeatureCell will now
// carry a feature tag and normalized message
`}}
